won: Balancing life support systems early creates a critical safety cushion for unforeseen space hazards.
Every operational decision in space exploration carries a real cost in power, oxygen, or shielding.
Careful resource stewardship allows human scientific research to thrive even on hostile worlds.
lost_oxygen: Colony air recycling loops must remain airtight; even small leaks or scrubber faults threaten crew survival.
Humans consume oxygen every single second, making scrubber maintenance and backup tanks top priorities.
When oxygen levels drop, astronaut focus and energy fall rapidly, making emergency repairs much harder.
lost_power: Extraterrestrial power grids depend on solar arrays that must be protected from dust, shadows, and freezing cold.
Power drives life support, heating, and oxygen generation—without electricity, all other colony systems shut down.
Managing battery reserves is essential to endure long planetary nights and solar eclipses.
lost_food: Hydroponic plants require carefully regulated light, moisture, and radiation shielding to produce calories.
Deep space outposts are too distant for emergency supply drops, making continuous food conservation essential.
Maintaining stable nutrition is required to keep astronaut energy, immune health, and mission morale high.
lost_shielding: Cosmic rays and solar storms deliver dangerous radiation doses unless stopped by thick regolith or water barriers.
Shielding degradation exposes both astronaut cells and fragile computer microchips to permanent damage.
Subsurface habitats and storm bunkers are essential protections against relentless deep-space radiation.
